1-2.word_for_word: aṣṭa-triṃśe — in the thirty-eighth chapter; yathā dhyāyan akrūraḥ gokulam gataḥ — how Akrūra went to Gokula while meditating; rāma-kṛṣṇābhyām gṛham nītvā su-satkṛtaḥ — how Rāma and Kṛṣṇa brought him home and honored him well; prātaḥ keśi-vadhe vṛtte — after Keśī's death in the morning; dvādaśyām nirgate munau — when the sage departed on the twelfth lunar day; tataḥ vyome hate — after Vyoma was killed; akrūraḥ sāyam gokulam āgamat — Akrūra reached Gokula in the evening; nāradena kaṃsa-vadha-ādi-kārye vijñāpite — after Nārada had informed him of the work beginning with Kaṃsa's death; śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ mathurām gantum udyataḥ — Śrī Kṛṣṇa was preparing to go to Mathurā
1-2.translation: The thirty-eighth chapter tells how Akrūra traveled to Gokula while meditating and how Rāma and Kṛṣṇa brought him into their home and honored him. Keśī was killed in the morning; on the twelfth lunar day Nārada departed; after Vyoma was then killed, Akrūra reached Gokula in the evening. Thus, after Nārada had informed Kṛṣṇa of the tasks beginning with the killing of Kaṃsa, Kṛṣṇa was preparing to go to Mathurā when Akrūra arrived in Gokula.

3.word_for_word: apiḥ — the particle api; sambhāvanāyām — expresses possibility or expectation; arhate — to one who is worthy; yogyāya — to one qualified
3.translation: The particle ‘api’ expresses possibility or hopeful expectation. ‘Arhate’ means ‘to one who is worthy or qualified.’

4.word_for_word: svasya kṛṣṇasya darśane asambhavam āśaṅkya — fearing that seeing Kṛṣṇa might be impossible for him; punaḥ sambhāvayati — he again considers it possible; viṣaya-ātmanaḥ — of one given to sense objects; viṣaya-āviṣṭa-cittasya — whose mind is absorbed in them; śūdrāt janma yasya tasya brahma-kīrtanam — Vedic recitation by one born from a śūdra; yathā — just as
4.translation: Akrūra first fears that the sight of Kṛṣṇa may be impossible for someone like himself, but in these two verses he again entertains hope. ‘Viṣayātman’ means one whose mind is immersed in objects of sense. His comparison is with Vedic recitation by one whose birth makes him unqualified for it: the hoped-for attainment seems similarly improbable.

5.word_for_word: mā evam — not so; adhamasya api mama syāt eva — even for lowly me it may indeed happen; hriyamāṇaḥ kāla-nadyā — carried along by the river of time; nadyā hriyamāṇānām tṛṇa-ādīnām madhye — among grasses and other things swept by a river; kiñcit kadācit tarati kūlam prāpnoti — something sometimes crosses and reaches the bank; karma-vaśena kālena hriyamāṇānām jīvānām madhye — among beings swept by time under the force of karma; kaścit taret — someone may cross
5.translation: Then he rejects the despair: ‘No; even for one as low as I am it may happen.’ Just as, among blades of grass and other things swept along by a river, one thing may by chance cross over and reach the bank, so among living beings carried along by time under the force of karma, someone may indeed cross beyond it.

6.word_for_word: anayā pravṛttyā eva — by this very undertaking; mama amaṅgalam dhruvam naṣṭam eva — my inauspiciousness is surely already destroyed; bhavaḥ janma ca sa-phalam jātam — my worldly existence and birth have become fruitful; yat yataḥ namaskariṣyāmi — because I shall bow down
6.translation: From the very fact that this journey has begun, Akrūra concludes that his misfortune must already have been destroyed. His birth and embodied existence have become fruitful, because he is going to bow down before Kṛṣṇa.

7.word_for_word: amaṅgala-nāśe sūcaka-antaram — another sign that misfortune has ended; bata — an expression of wonder; ati-khalaḥ kaṃsaḥ api — even the extremely wicked Kaṃsa; mama atyantam anugraham kṛtavān — has done me a supreme favor; amunā kaṃsena prahitaḥ — sent by that Kaṃsa; hareḥ aṅghri-padmam drakṣye — I shall see Hari's lotus feet; pūrve ambarīṣa-ādayaḥ tamaḥ saṃsāram ataran — formerly Ambarīṣa and others crossed the darkness of saṃsāra through them
7.translation: He sees another sign that his misfortune has ended: ‘Amazing! Even the extremely wicked Kaṃsa has bestowed the greatest favor on me, because by sending me he has enabled me to behold Hari's lotus feet.’ Those very feet enabled Ambarīṣa and other devotees of old to cross the darkness of saṃsāra.

8.word_for_word: aṅghri-padmam vibhāvayati — he contemplates those lotus feet; brahma-ādibhiḥ arcitam — worshiped by Brahmā and others; parama-aiśvaryam — supreme sovereignty; śriyā ca — and by Śrī; saubhāgya-atiśayam — unsurpassed blessedness; munibhiḥ bhakta-sahitaiḥ — by sages together with devotees; parama-puruṣārthatvam — being the supreme human goal; go-cāraṇāya — for tending the cows; kṛpālutvam — compassion; gopikānām — of the gopīs; prema-mātra-sulabhatvam — obtainable by love alone
8.translation: Akrūra contemplates the lotus feet. Their worship by Brahmā and the other gods expresses Kṛṣṇa's supreme sovereignty; their service by Śrī expresses unsurpassed blessedness; their worship by sages and devotees shows that they are the supreme goal of life; their going out to herd cows shows his compassion; and their relation to the gopīs shows that he is attainable simply through love.

9.word_for_word: manoratha-antaram karoti — he forms another longing; śobhamānau kapolau nāsikā ca yasmin — whose cheeks and nose are beautiful; smita-sahitaḥ avalokaḥ yasmin — whose glance is accompanied by a smile; aruṇa-kañja-vat locane — eyes like reddish lotuses; guḍālaka-āvṛtam — covered by curling locks; vakra-keśa-āvṛtam — framed by curly hair; pradakṣiṇam — an auspicious sign on the right
9.translation: Akrūra forms another longing: to see Kṛṣṇa's face, with its beautiful cheeks and nose, its smiling glance, eyes like reddish lotuses, and curling locks of hair. Seeing at that very moment an auspicious sign on his right, he becomes intensely joyful and says, ‘auspiciously on the right.’

10.word_for_word: apy adya — perhaps today; iyuṣaḥ — of one who has attained; lāvaṇyasya dhāma-āśrayaḥ tasya viṣṇoḥ — Viṣṇu, the abode of beauty; yad vā viṣṇoḥ lāvaṇya-yuktam dhāma vapuḥ — or Viṣṇu's form, the dwelling of beauty; upalambhanam — seeing, obtaining sight; bhavitā — will occur; dṛśaḥ phalam — the fruit of my eyesight
10.translation: He thinks further: ‘Perhaps today I shall obtain the sight of Viṣṇu, the very abode in which beauty resides—or of that body of Viṣṇu which is beauty's own dwelling. If this happens, my eyes will indeed attain their true fruit.’

11.word_for_word: ya īkṣita iti ādi caturbhiḥ — a four-verse unit beginning ‘he who sees’; bhoktṛtva-kartṛtva-ādi-dharmaiḥ pratīyamānasya katham viṣṇutvam — how can one who appears to possess agency and enjoyership like us be Viṣṇu?; asat-satoḥ kārya-kāraṇayoḥ īkṣitā — the observer of effect and cause; īkṣaṇa-mātra-kartā api ahaṃkāra-rahitaḥ — though merely causing by seeing, free of ego; apāsta-tamo-bhidā-bhramaḥ — ignorance, differentiation and consequent delusion removed; sva-tejasā cit-śaktyā — by his own radiance, conscious potency; nitya-svarūpa-sākṣātkāreṇa — through eternal self-realization; sva-māyayā — through his own controlled māyā; prāṇa-akṣa-dhībhiḥ sahitaiḥ jīvaiḥ — with living beings endowed with life, senses and intelligence; ātmani svasmin eva racitaiḥ — fashioned within himself; sadaneṣu — in dwellings; līlayā karmāṇi kurvan — performing acts in play; sakta-vat abhīyate — appears as though attached
11.translation: The four verses beginning ‘He who sees’ form a single unit. A doubt arises: if Kṛṣṇa appears, like ordinary beings, to act and enjoy in various ways, how can he be Viṣṇu? The next three verses remove this doubt, and the fourth returns to Akrūra's longing to see him. Kṛṣṇa is merely the witnessing seer of both cause and effect; even where his seeing brings about creation, he is devoid of ego. In him ignorance, the perception of separateness born from it, and the resulting fixation or delusion have all been removed by his own radiance—his conscious potency and eternal direct awareness of his own nature. Yet through his own māyā, which remains under his control, he fashions within himself living beings endowed with life, senses and intellect, and in the dwellings of Vṛndāvana, including its trees and the homes of the gopīs, he performs activities as play, appearing as though attached to them.

12.word_for_word: sarvathā ahaṃkāra-ādi-rahitasya ātmārāmasya līlā api kutaḥ — if he is entirely free from ego and self-satisfied, why does he perform līlā?; para-anugraha-arthā — for the grace of others; akhila-amīva-hāni — destroying all sins or the sins of all; su-maṅgalaiḥ — producing excellent auspiciousness; guṇāḥ karuṇā-ādayaḥ karmāṇi janmāni ca — qualities such as compassion, deeds and births; taiḥ vemiśrāḥ vācaḥ — speech interwoven with them; jagat prāṇanti śumbhanti punanti — gives life to, beautifies and purifies the world; tair viraktāḥ — speech devoid of them; sva-alaṅkṛtā api — although ornamented by itself; vastra-ādi-alaṅkṛta-śava-vat — like a corpse adorned with clothing; satām asammatāḥ — not approved by the good
12.translation: One might ask why a completely egoless and self-satisfied Lord engages in līlā at all. The answer is that it is for the grace of others. Words joined with accounts of his qualities such as compassion, his deeds and his descents destroy every sin, produce the highest auspiciousness, give life to the world, beautify it and purify it. By contrast, speech devoid of those subjects, however elegantly ornamented, is regarded by the good as no better than a corpse decorated with clothing and ornaments.

13.word_for_word: svayam racitān setūn — boundaries established by himself; varṇāśrama-dharmān — duties of varṇa and āśrama; pālayatām amara-varyāṇām — of the chief gods who preserve them; sukha-kartā san — bringing them well-being; avatīrṇaḥ — descended; yad yaśaḥ — whose fame
13.translation: He has descended to bring well-being to the foremost gods who preserve the boundaries he himself established, namely the duties of varṇa and āśrama. The verse proceeds to speak of his fame.

14.word_for_word: trailokye ekam eva kāntam — the uniquely beautiful one in the three worlds; dṛśimatām mahān utsavaḥ — a great festival for those who possess sight; yad vā mahān utsava eva — or itself the great festival; śriyaḥ īpsitam āspadam — the abode desired by Śrī; rūpam śrī-mūrtim dadhānam — bearing such a beautiful divine form; su-darśanāḥ uṣasaḥ — auspiciously beautiful dawns; sukham prabhātāḥ rajanyaḥ — nights ending pleasantly in dawn; śubha-sūcikāḥ — indicating good fortune
14.translation: He is the one uniquely beautiful being in the three worlds, a great festival for all who have eyes—or rather, himself the very embodiment of such a festival—and the abode desired by Śrī. Akrūra longs to see the Lord bearing that divine form. The favorable signs confirm his hope: the dawns were beautiful and auspicious, and the nights ended pleasantly, indicating good fortune.

15.word_for_word: darśana-anantaram — immediately after seeing him; sapadi tat-kṣaṇam eva — at once, that very moment; rathāt avatīrṇaḥ — descending from the chariot; pradhānayoḥ puruṣayoḥ rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ caraṇam — the feet of the two foremost persons, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa; yogibhiḥ api ātma-lābhāya dhiyā eva dhṛtam — held in meditation even by yogīs for realization of the Self; sākṣāt aham namasyāmi — I shall bow to them directly; sakhīn gopān ca — and to their cowherd companions
15.translation: Akrūra thinks: ‘Immediately upon seeing them, I shall descend from the chariot and directly bow to the feet of the two foremost persons, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa—the very feet that yogīs hold only in meditation in order to attain the Self. I shall also bow to their cowherd friends.’

16.word_for_word: adhāsyat — will place; dhāsyati — he will place; dttābhayam iti — the phrase ‘which grants fearlessness’; sārdhena — explained through the following half-verse
16.translation: ‘Adhāsyat’ has the future sense ‘he will place.’ Akrūra then contemplates that hand in the following verse and a half, beginning with the description ‘which grants fearlessness.’

17.word_for_word: balinā — by Bali; pada-traya-parimita-bhū-dāna-samaye — when donating the earth measured by three steps; tasya haste udakam nihitam — water was placed in that hand; kauśikaḥ indraḥ — Indra, descendant of Kuśika; tenā api kadācit kiñcit nihitam — he too once placed something there; mumukṣūṇām saṃsāra-bhaya-nivartakam — removing fear of saṃsāra for seekers of liberation; sa-kāmānām abhyudaya-pradam — granting prosperity to those with desires; anuraktānām parama-sukham — supreme joy for those in love; vihāre rāsa-krīḍāyām — in the sport of the rāsa; saugandhika-gandhi — fragrant like the saugandhika flower
17.translation: At the time Bali gave the earth measured by three steps, the ceremonial water was placed in that hand; Indra too, the Kauśika, is understood to have once placed an offering there. That hand removes the fear of saṃsāra for those seeking liberation and grants worldly flourishing to those who desire it. For those bound to Kṛṣṇa by love it gives something greater still: supreme joy. During the rāsa pastime it became fragrant like the saugandhika flower.

18.word_for_word: parama-anugraham sambhāvya — having hoped for this supreme favor; punaḥ asambhavam āśaṅkya — again fearing it may be impossible; kaṃsena prahitaḥ — sent by Kaṃsa; tasya dūtaḥ — his messenger; mayi areḥ ayam iti buddhim na upaiṣyati — he will not think of me as an enemy; viśva-dṛk — seer of all; sarva-jñaḥ — omniscient; cetasaḥ antaḥ ca bahiḥ ca yad īhitam — whatever is intended inwardly and outwardly in my mind; kṣetra-jñaḥ antaryāmī — knower of the field, indwelling controller; nitya-jñānena īkṣate — sees through eternal knowledge; bahiḥ kaṃsam anuvartate antaḥ kṛṣṇam eva — outwardly I follow Kaṃsa, inwardly only Kṛṣṇa
18.translation: After imagining this supreme favor, Akrūra again fears that it may not occur, then removes the doubt: ‘Although Kaṃsa sent me and I am therefore outwardly his messenger, Kṛṣṇa will not think, “This man belongs to my enemy.” He sees the whole universe and knows all. As the knower of the field and the indwelling Lord, he eternally perceives everything intended and done both within and outside my mind. Outwardly I comply with Kaṃsa; inwardly I belong only to Kṛṣṇa. He who dwells in my heart knows this.’ Alternatively, the phrase can refer to all activity of the universe.

19.word_for_word: aṅghri-mūle avahitam — composed and attentive at the base of his feet; kṛpā-amṛtena ārdrayā dṛśā — with a glance moistened by the nectar of compassion; mām īkṣitā — if he should look upon me; sapadi vinaṣṭa-akhila-kalmaṣaḥ — immediately freed from every stain; parām mudam voḍhā — I shall obtain supreme joy
19.translation: ‘If, while I remain composed at his feet, he looks upon me with a glance moistened by the nectar of compassion, all my sins will vanish at once and I shall attain supreme joy.’

20.word_for_word: atha mām parirapsyate — then he will embrace me; me ātmā dehaḥ tīrthī-kriyate — my body will be made into a holy place; ati-pavitrī-kariṣyate — it will be made supremely pure; ucchvasiti — will relax, breathe freely; ślathaḥ bhaviṣyati — will become loosened; ataḥ dehāt — from bodily tension
20.translation: ‘Then he will embrace me. At that very moment my body will be transformed into a holy place, made utterly pure, and the tension of embodied existence will loosen as I breathe freely.’

21.word_for_word: tat janma-bhṛtaḥ — those whose birth is such; sa-phala-janmānaḥ — whose birth has become fruitful; anyathā tat janma eva na bhavati — otherwise such a life scarcely counts as birth; mahīyasā śrī-kṛṣṇena yaḥ anādṛtaḥ — one disregarded by the exalted Śrī Kṛṣṇa; amuṣya jantoḥ tat janma dhik — shame upon that creature's birth
21.translation: Those who receive such grace have truly made their birth fruitful. Indeed, without it, birth itself is scarcely worthy of the name: ‘Shame upon the life of that creature who is disregarded by the exalted Śrī Kṛṣṇa.’

22.word_for_word: pariṣvaṅga-saṃpraśna-ādayaḥ jīva-dharmāḥ katham īśvare — how can embracing, asking after welfare and similar traits of finite beings apply to the Lord?; dayitaḥ — beloved; apriyaḥ — disliked; suhṛttamaḥ — greatest well-wisher; dveṣyaḥ — hated; upekṣyaḥ — indifferent; dayita-ādayaḥ na santi iti satyam — it is true that such partial categories do not exist for him; tathā api bhaktān bhajate — yet he reciprocates with devotees; ye yathā mām prapadyante tān tathā eva bhajāmi — ‘as they approach me, so I reciprocate with them’; sura-druma-vat — like a celestial wish-fulfilling tree
22.translation: One might object that embracing someone, asking about his welfare and similar actions belong to ordinary embodied beings; how can they apply to the Lord? The answer is that Kṛṣṇa has no intrinsically beloved person, disliked person, supreme friend, enemy or one whom he merely ignores. That is true. Yet he reciprocates with devotees precisely according to their approach, in accordance with his declaration, ‘As they surrender to me, so I reciprocate with them.’ Although impartial, he gives fruit to devotees just as a celestial wish-fulfilling tree gives according to what is sought from it.

23.word_for_word: yaḥ mayā añjaliḥ kariṣyate — the joined palms I shall form; tasmin eva añjalau gṛhītam mām — me taken within those very joined hands; āptāni samastāni arghya-ādi-satkṛtāni yena — by whom all honors beginning with arghya have thereby been received
23.translation: Akrūra imagines that when he forms his palms in reverence, Kṛṣṇa will take him by those very joined hands. In doing so, Kṛṣṇa will count as having accepted from him every honor beginning with the offering of arghya.

24.word_for_word: saḥ tu mārgam api na veda — he did not even know the road; tathā api rathena prāptaḥ — nevertheless he reached the place by chariot
24.translation: Although Akrūra did not even know the road, he nevertheless reached Gokula in his chariot.

25.word_for_word: akhilaiḥ loka-pālaiḥ — by all guardians of the worlds; kirīṭeṣu juṣṭāḥ — received upon their crowns; amalāḥ pāda-reṇavaḥ yasya — whose stainless foot-dust; kṣiti-kautukāni — wonders of the earth; kṣiteḥ alaṅkāra-rūpāṇi — ornaments of the earth
25.translation: The spotless dust of those feet is borne upon the crowns of all the guardians of the worlds. Their marks upon the ground are ‘wonders of the earth,’ that is, ornaments adorning the earth itself.

26.word_for_word: tad-darśanena teṣām padānām darśanena yaḥ āhlādaḥ — the joy produced by seeing those footprints; tena vivṛddhaḥ sambhramaḥ yasya — whose excitement increased through it; premṇā ūrdhvāni romāṇi — hairs standing erect with love; aśrūṇām kalābhiḥ ākule īkṣaṇe — eyes filled with traces of tears; avaskandya avaplutya — jumping down; teṣu padeṣu acesṭata vyaluṭhat — he rolled upon those footprints; aho iti durlabhatām bhāvayan — exclaiming ‘Ah!’ while contemplating their rarity
26.translation: At the sight of those footprints Akrūra's joyful excitement increased. His hairs stood erect with love and his eyes filled with tears. Leaping down from the chariot, he rolled upon the footprints, exclaiming ‘Ah!’ as he contemplated how rare such contact was.

27.word_for_word: kim-artham evam vyaluṭhat — why did he roll upon the ground like this?; prema-saṃrambhe phala-uddeśaḥ na asti — in the intensity of love there is no calculating aim at a result; deha-bhājām etāvān eva puruṣārthaḥ — this alone is the supreme goal of embodied beings; kaṃsasya sandeśāt ārabhya — beginning with Kaṃsa's message; hareḥ liṅga-darśana-śravaṇa-ādibhiḥ — through seeing and hearing the signs of Hari; akrūrasya varṇitaḥ — the state of Akrūra described here
27.translation: Why did Akrūra roll on the ground in this way? Intense love acts without calculating any result. For embodied beings, this very state is itself the highest human goal. The transformation described in Akrūra, beginning with Kaṃsa's message and growing through hearing and seeing the signs of Hari, culminates here. Alternatively, the wording means that this entire attainment, whose first occasion was Kaṃsa's message, had now arisen in Akrūra.

28.word_for_word: tataḥ kṛṣṇam rāmam ca dadarśa — then he saw Kṛṣṇa and Rāma; gāvaḥ duhyante asmin iti go-dohanam — ‘cow-milking place’ is the place where cows are milked; tat-sthānam gatau prāptau — they had reached that place
28.translation: Then Akrūra saw Kṛṣṇa and Rāma. ‘Go-dohana’ means the place where the cows are milked; the two brothers had come to that spot.

30.word_for_word: anukrośaḥ — compassion; anukampā — pity, tenderness; tad-vilasita-smita-yuktam īkṣaṇam yayoḥ — whose glances were accompanied by smiles expressive of that compassion
30.translation: ‘Anukrośa’ means compassion or tender sympathy. Their glances were accompanied by smiles expressive of that compassion.

31.word_for_word: udārā rucirā krīḍā yayoḥ — whose play was noble and beautiful; sragviṇau — wearing garlands; ratna-sragbhiḥ alaṅkṛtau — adorned with jeweled garlands
31.translation: Their play was noble and beautiful. ‘Sragviṇau’ means that the two were adorned with garlands, here jeweled garlands.

32.word_for_word: pradhāna-bhūtau puruṣau — the two principal Persons; prakṛti-puruṣa-ātmakau vā — or embodying Prakṛti and Puruṣa; ādyau — primordial; jagad-hetū — causes of the universe; jagat-patī — lords of the universe; viparītaḥ vā — or the causal sequence may be read in reverse; pṛthivyā bhāra-apanayanāya — to remove the burden of the earth; sva-aṃśena mūrti-bhedena — through distinct manifestations of their own portions; bala-keśavau santau avatīrṇau — descended as Balarāma and Keśava
32.translation: They are the two principal Persons; alternatively, they may be understood as embodying Prakṛti and Puruṣa. They are primordial, and from that follows their being causes of the universe and therefore its Lords; or the causal relation among these descriptions may be understood in the reverse order. For the sake of the world—specifically to remove the burden of the earth—they descended in distinct manifestations as Balarāma and Keśava.

33.word_for_word: sva-prabhayā — by their own radiance; vigata-timitāḥ diśaḥ kurvāṇau — making the directions free of darkness; kanaka-ācitau — covered in gold; suvarṇa-vyāptau — adorned throughout with gold; sa-alaṅkārayoḥ śaila-sādṛśya-artham — said to establish the comparison of the ornamented pair with mountains
33.translation: By their own radiance they drove darkness from the directions. The description ‘covered with gold’ means adorned throughout with golden ornaments and is used to support the comparison of the magnificently adorned brothers with mountains.

35.word_for_word: bhagavad-darśana-āhlādena yad bāṣpam — the tears born from the joy of seeing Bhagavān; tena paryākule īkṣaṇe — eyes overwhelmed by them; pulakaiḥ ācitam aṅgam — body covered with horripilation; sva-khyāne — in stating his own identity; akrūraḥ aham namaskaromi — ‘I am Akrūra; I bow to you’; kathane na aśaknot — he was unable to say it
35.translation: The joy of seeing Bhagavān filled Akrūra's eyes with tears, and horripilation covered his body. He could not even state his own identity by saying, ‘I am Akrūra; I bow to you.’

36.word_for_word: abhipretya — understanding his intention; akrūraḥ ayam etad-artham āgataḥ iti jñātvā — knowing that Akrūra had come for this purpose; kaṃsa-hanana-sāmarthyam dyotayan iva — as though indicating his power to kill Kaṃsa; rathāṅgena cakreṇa aṅkitaḥ pāṇiḥ — the hand marked with the wheel; tena abhyupākṛṣya — drawing him close with it; tam āliṅgitavān — embraced him
36.translation: Knowing Akrūra's intention and understanding that he had come on Kaṃsa's business, Kṛṣṇa drew him near with the hand marked by the discus and embraced him, as though thereby indicating his own power to destroy Kaṃsa.

37.word_for_word: pāṇī — the two hands; añjali-rūpeṇa saṃhitau eva — still joined in the form of reverence; gṛhītvā — taking them
37.translation: Rāma took Akrūra's two hands while they were still joined together in reverence.

38.word_for_word: madhu-parkaḥ eva arhaṇam — the madhuparka itself is the formal honor; tasmin vā yad ucitam arhaṇam — or the appropriate honor accompanying it; āharat — brought; ānīya samarpitavān — brought it and offered it
38.translation: The ‘honor’ may mean the madhuparka itself, or the appropriate offerings connected with it. The sense is that they brought these items and presented them to Akrūra.

41.word_for_word: sat-kṛtam — honored; sammānitam — respectfully received; niranugrahe — devoid of compassion; krūre — cruel; katham kena prakāreṇa stha jīvatha — how, in what manner, do you remain alive?; saunaḥ — animal slaughterer; sa eva pālakaḥ yeṣām avīnām — sheep whose protector is himself their slaughterer; te iva — like those
41.translation: ‘Sat-kṛta’ means honored and respectfully received. Kṛṣṇa asks how they can continue to live under one who is merciless and cruel. The comparison is with sheep whose very keeper is also their slaughterer.

42.word_for_word: niranugrahatām āha — he explains that lack of compassion; tokān — children; asu-tṛp — one who satisfies himself with lives; asūn eva tarpayati yaḥ — one who feeds upon life itself; ataḥ khalaḥ — therefore wicked; tasya kaṃsasya prajānām — of Kaṃsa's subjects; yeṣām jīvana-mātram api durlabham — for whom mere survival is difficult; vaḥ kim nu kuśalam vicārayāmaḥ — how can we even inquire whether you are well?
42.translation: The next verse explains Kaṃsa's mercilessness. ‘Tokān’ means children. ‘Asu-tṛp’ means one who gratifies himself with the very lives of others; hence Kaṃsa is wicked. ‘O Akrūra, when even bare survival is difficult for the subjects of such a king, how can we meaningfully ask whether you are well?’

43.word_for_word: madhurayā vācā — with sweet speech; ittham sat-kṛtaḥ — honored in this way; tathā eva vācā paripṛṣṭena praśnena — questioned with equally gracious words; adhva-pariśramam — fatigue of the journey; saṃsāra-śramam — or the weariness of worldly existence
43.translation: Thus Akrūra was honored with sweet words and questioned with equally gracious speech. ‘Fatigue of the road’ may also suggest the deeper weariness of saṃsāra.
